series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #29 (invisible progress)
hook: You're getting better. You just can't see it.

gate.goal_link: any skill goal (singing): quitting because progress feels flat
gate.mechanism: day-to-day change is below what you can notice; you compare with yesterday, so progress only shows against an old fixed benchmark. No study cited; bars are an illustration.
gate.universal: practising daily and feeling no better

frame.obstacle: two months of 20 min a day, every day sounds like the day before
frame.cost: almost quit after 60 days (~20 hours of practice)
frame.fix: the Sunday test: same song, same minute, same key every Sunday, never delete; at week 8 play week 1 first. Running: same 2 km timed; writing: same prompt 10 min

hooks_considered.line: You're getting better. You just can't see it.
hooks_considered.checks: hard truth Y, gap Y (why not?), muted Y (40% vs 1% bars), sendable Y

hooks_considered.line: Most people quit right before they could hear the difference.
Yesterday is the worst thing to compare yourself to.

beats.hard_truth: 0.0 s bars better than week 1 40% vs better than yesterday 1%
